newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ govt to power market - get competitive, or else!
newsitem.headline: NZ govt to power market - get competitive, or else!

text.p: New Zealand Energy Minister Max Bradford on Wednesday warned electricity industry participants to deliver a competitive market, or the government would consider further splitting state-owned generator ECNZ.

In a speech to industry officials gathered for a winter solstice celebration, Bradford said the government also considered splitting power companies' distribution and retail functions into separate entities in the pursuit of a competitive market.
"I want to see a market with with strong downward pressure on costs and efficient prices," he said.
"In order to deliver these, there must be effective competition in all areas of the market, from generation to the wholesale market and retailing.

"Barriers to entry must be removed, access to grid and distribution lines must be open with unbundled and transparent costs. There is still a great deal to be done before I am satisfied with the state of our electricity industry."
Bradford said he had commissioned a study on ways to promote retail competition and drive competition as far down as possible through the retail market.
"If there are suggestions that competitive outcomes are not being delivered, then further steps to increase competition will be increasingly prominent in my thinking," he said.
"The possibility of further splitting ECNZ has not been forgotten. Generators must do their part in ensuring competitive outcomes.
"Ideally, a market should contain no single dominant player."
The government split ECNZ 70/30 in 1995 to form Contact Energy with the smaller portion. Both state-owned generators are expected to compete with each other in the wholesale market.
Bradford said he had also not ruled out the possibility of splitting power companies' distribution and retail functions into separate entities.

"It seems to me such a move might be the way to keep things simple and circumvent the possibities of creative accounting which blurs the boundaries between their line and retail businesses under the current information disclosure regime," he said.
"The reduction in barriers to competition must become a key focus of the entire industry if it wishes to remain the least regulated in the world."
New Zealand launched a wholesale electricity market on October 1 last year designed to foster competition in all areas of the industry.
